page.layout: One page of text, one column, centred; two engraved medallions with inscriptions at the top (not transcribed as text, described under notes); running head at the top; page number at the top left; no margin notes.

main_text.p: ORITHYA, Marthesiæ filia, Amazonum post matrem Regina, tum ob belli industriam, tum ob perpetuam virginitatem, conspicuam se, ac mirabilem præstitit. Hæc vbi coperit bellum, vim quoque sororibus suis illatam ab Hercule & Theseo, hortatur comites in vltionē, frustráque Ponti sinum & Asiam domitam esse dicit, si Græcorum non tam bellis quàm rapinis pateant. auxiliū à Rege Scytharum capit. Sed ante prœliū dis-sensione orta, ab auxiliis desertæ Amazones, bellóq; ab Athe-niésibus victæ, receptaculum tamen habuere castra sociorum, in regnúmque reuersæ sunt. Iustin. lib. 2.
main_text.head: PENTHESILEA post Orythiam Amazonis imperauit. Hæc Troianis aduersus Græcos opem tulit. Verg. lib. Aen. 1.
main_text.l: Penthesilea furens, mediisque in millibus ardet,
main_text.p: Interfecta demum ab Achille, exercitúque eius absumpto, paucæ quæ remanserant vsque ad tempora Alexandri Magni durauerunt: quem Thalestris, Amazonum Regina, adiit, ad sobolem ex eo generandam. Hunc cum ter centum feminis salutauit, cæteris iussis subsistere, copiam sui fecit ei Alexander per tredecim dies. Hæc coram illi in os ingenuè fassa est se tantum ad suscipiēdos liberos venisse: fœminini sexus se retenturam, marem patri redditurā. reuersa in regnum, breui pòst tempore cum omni Amazonum nomine intercidit. Quint. Curt. lib. 6. Iustin. lib. 2. de hac vide etiam infra in Alexandro.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions (coins) above the text: left, a helmeted female head in profile facing right, inscribed "ORITHYA ΑΜΑ" (partly legible, around the rim); right, a female head in profile facing right with a diadem, inscribed "ΠΕΝΘΑΣΙΛΕΑ" with "ΑΜ" at the left rim. The inscriptions are not transcribed as text because they are part of the illustration. The Latin headings "ORITHYA" and "PENTHESILEA" are set in capitals; "PENTHESILEA" is treated as a level 2 heading. The verse lines are italic. Some printed letters in the first paragraph are slightly faded but legible.
